author: Matt Margolis
title: More Bad News for Democrats I'm Happy to Deliver - PJ Media
text:
Democrats have spent the better part of a year counting down to November 2026 like kids counting down to Christmas morning. This is supposed to be their moment. Win back the House, fire up the subpoenas, dig up something, anything, no matter how stupid, to investigate President Donald Trump, and maybe even try impeachment a third time. It's a nice fantasy. Reality just keeps on kneecapping it.
The 2026 midterms were always going to shape the final two years of Trump's presidency. The math is quite simple: either Republicans hold Congress and the Trump agenda marches on, or Democrats claw back the House and turn Washington into an investigation factory.
Do I know what will happen in November? Of course not. But I know things are going to be a lot harder for Democrats than they realize. New mid-decade redistricting has helped level the playing field significantly, so Democrats now need to win the national popular vote by three to four points to retake the House in 2026, which is much different than the single point they needed before. CNN's Harry Enten broke down the shift, explaining that under the old lines, Democrats needed only a combined 1-point national vote advantage to seize control of the House.
"And you can see here the national vote margin Dems need to win the House control," Enten said. "Well under the current lines, right, the lines that are happening right now, they only would have to have won the National House popular vote by less than a point, by less than a point. So basically any win would have gotten them the House. But now with redistricting, look at this, the Democrats in order to win back the House of Representatives, they have to win by anywhere from three all the way up to four percentage points. So Democrats can't just win by a little, they got to win by a lot to win back the House."
🚨 BREAKING: CNN has just admitted that Democrats need to win the 2026 national popular vote by +3-4 POINTS because of GOP redistricting
— Eric Daugherty (@EricLDaugh)
Before this, they only needed 1 point! 🤯
"To win House control, under current lines...they only would have to have won by less than 1…[pic.twitter.com/R9gcup6VjC][August 17, 2026]
For months, analysts had been promising Democrats a "blue tsunami" in 2026, leaning on the old rule that the party holding the White House loses congressional seats in the midterms. In fact, that rule of thumb is exactly why so many Democrats assumed this would be easy. Obviously, nobody building those forecasts factored in a redistricting overhaul that would move the goalposts by three whole points.
President Trump made holding Republican control of Congress a top priority well before any of this played out, and it is starting to pay off. The GOP's odds heading into 2026 look considerably better than anyone expected a year ago.

Democrats never expected that after decades of gerrymandering safe blue districts nationwide, Republicans would ever fight back to balance things out. Well, it’s a new Republican Party under Donald Trump. Of course, Democrats tried to answer with redistricting pushes of their own. Several of those efforts either collapsed outright or backfired on the party that drew them.
Make no mistake about it: Democrats still have history on their side heading into the midterm election. But history is about the only thing they have going for them right now. The gerrymandered edge that once made a narrow national win enough to flip the House is gone. Republicans also have a fundraising edge that will be a major help in the final weeks.
The midterms will decide whether Trump's agenda keeps moving or stalls out, and Democrats are walking into that fight needing far more than they bargained for.
